root_cause.text: The `tap_get_user_xdp()` function fails to release page-fragment memory allocated by `vhost_net_build_xdp()` when rejecting frames shorter than ETH_HLEN or when `build_skb()` fails, causing page leaks because `tap_sendmsg()` masks error returns and always reports success to the caller.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `put_page(virt_to_head_page(xdp->data))` calls before both error paths (the ETH_HLEN validation check and the `build_skb()` failure case). The CVE description explicitly states that "tap_sendmsg() discards the per-buffer return value and always returns 0, so vhost_tx_batch() takes the success path and never frees the page; each rejected frame in a batch leaks one page-frag chunk." This indicates the root cause is the missing page deallocation combined with error masking at the caller level, resulting in unreleased memory on error conditions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix page reference leak in tap_get_user_xdp() by releasing the page on early validation failure.
intent_record.what: Added a `put_page(virt_to_head_page(xdp->data))` call before the error return in the early validation check of `tap_get_user_xdp()` function.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that when an XDP buffer has insufficient data (less than Ethernet header length), the reference count of the underlying page is decremented before returning an error. Without this, the page reference acquired earlier would leak, causing the page to remain pinned in memory indefinitely.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix page reference leak in tap_get_user_xdp() by releasing the page when build_skb() allocation fails.
intent_record.what: Added a `put_page(virt_to_head_page(xdp->data))` call in the error path when `build_skb()` fails to allocate memory in the `tap_get_user_xdp()` function.
intent_record.how: When `build_skb()` returns NULL, the code now releases the reference to the page associated with the XDP buffer's data before returning the error. This prevents a page reference leak that would otherwise occur when the function exits via the error path without properly decrementing the page's reference count.

bic_trace_step.reason: The `tap_get_user_xdp()` function introduced in this commit has a critical memory leak vulnerability. The function allocates page-fragment memory via `build_skb(xdp->data_hard_start, buflen)` at line 1160, but fails to properly release it in all error paths. Specifically: (1) There is no check for frames shorter than ETH_HLEN before or after `build_skb()`, so undersized frames will leak the allocated buffer. (2) When `build_skb()` fails at line 1160-1162, the function jumps to `err` label which does not free the xdp buffer - only increments drop counter. (3) The `tap_sendmsg()` function at lines 1220-1226 calls `tap_get_user_xdp()` in a loop but ignores its return value (line 1224: `tap_get_user_xdp(q, xdp);` result is discarded), and always returns 0 at line 1225, masking any errors to the caller. This means even if errors occur, the caller believes the operation succeeded. The vulnerable construct is present: memory allocated by `build_skb()` can be leaked when `build_skb()` fails or when frames are too short, and the error handling does not properly release the xdp buffer resources.
